properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Swn Prod Co Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-07-09
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 888537
Permit API: 117-21931
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-07-09
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a report of elevated conductivity fluid discovered on the pad on 7/7/20. Dillon Otten reported on 7/7/20 that fluid with electrical conductivity (EC) between 11-12 mS/cm was discovered during excavation adjacent to the 2H well head. An estimated release volume was provided of 42 gallons. Four wells were recently fraced and completed on this pad. These wells were being plumbed into the production equipment on the pad at the time of this inspection. Four existing wells are present on the pad and in production. Upon arriving on location, I observed the trench adjacent to the 2H well head. A sump was present close to the well head and a small puddle was present within the sump. No fluid was observed flowing into or out of the sump. The other areas in the trench were dry. No staining or puddles were present on the pad surface. The fluid in the sump had an EC of 15.06 mS/cm. Due to the reported spill volume of 42 gallons, Act 2 remediation is required by 78a.66. The Department recommends investigating the source of the elevated conductivity fluid. Violations noted.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/26/2023
Violation Code: 78a66(b)2 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases - Operator or other responsible party failed to contact the appropriate regional Department office by telephone or call the Department’s Statewide toll free number as soon as practicable, but no later than 2 hours after discovering the spill or release.
Violation ID: 992564
Permit API: 015-23753
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Terry Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 4/26/2023
Comments: On 4/26/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an Administrative inspection on the Chesapeake Grippo well site. This inspection is to report the results of one water sample that was collected from a 60' x 60' water/ice puddle that was located southeast of the well heads and adjacent to the south edge of secondary containment for six frac tanks.During an inspection on 3/30/2023, the department discovered elevated conductance fluid on the well pad surface outside of containment. The fluid covered a 60' x 60' area and field tested at 4.05 mS conductance with an Oakton PCTS-50 meter. The department collected water sample #9551-049 for laboratory analysis from location Lat: 41.64109 Long: -76.35054. On 4/20/2023 the department received the results of the laboratory analysis that shows elevated barium, strontium, lithium and chlorides and is indicative of brine/production fluid being released onto the pad. The sample report is displayed in pictures 5 and 6. Chesapeake is pursuing Act 2 for the site in response to that incident.The release of fluid with elevated conductance to the pad surface during production operations constitutes violations of SWMA 301, CSL 402, 25 PA Code 78a.57(a) and 78a.66(b)(2).Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3529982 for elevated conductance fluid being discovered on the unprotected pad surface and for inspection ID 3517519 for high conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface after fracking operations and for elevated conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface during drilling operations.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/26/2023
Violation Code: 78.81(a)1 - CASING AND CEMENTING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Operator conducted casing and cementing activities that failed to allow for effective control of the well at all times.
Violation ID: 1001072
Permit API: 083-53811
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Foster Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/11/2023
Comments: Well inspection conducted as an ongoing gas migration investigation and a follow up inspection after methane was detected in the ground outside the surface casing. On 7/11/23 three slam bar holes were placed in the ground 1'-2' from the well bore. 42% LEL was detected in one of the three slam bar holes. The casing pressure gauge read 0 P.S.I. Tubing pressure gauge indicated 38 P.S.I. A violation was submitted on 7/13/2023. This violation occurred on 4/26/2023 but due to possible technical complications on the Subsair application, the inspection was never submitted to the operator until July 13, 2023. Comments: On site inspection conducted to review overall pad conditions and to inspect the two Select Energy Services 22K/26K Modular Aboveground Storage Structure (MASS) in use for well stimulation operations. Meeting on site today with Greylock Consultant Brandon Mitchell. Weather conditions at time of inspection are overcast and 24 degrees F. The site is snow and ice covered due to recent precipitation. According to Mr. Mitchell, a Halliburton frac operation is currently conducting well stimulation operations on the 1UH Utica well (API#105-21963). The crew is on stage 7 of 100 on the first well of two on site. Stimulation activity is expected to take around three more weeks. The north MASS is holding produced fluid offloaded from trucks, while the south MASS has production fluid blended with freshwater prior to transferring to tanks adjacent to the frac equipment. Each MASS is holding approximately 8,000 barrels at time of inspection. On pad fluid transfer of production fluid from trucks to the MASS Is conducted on secondary containment with rig mats (photo 2). During this inspection, the Department screened puddles broken through ice within and outside containment structures for elevated conductivity using an Oakton PCTS50 meter. No evidence of spills or produced fluid leaks are observed from the MASS's, fluid transfer lines, or pumping and valves at time of inspection.There are no new violations and no violations associated with Modular Aboveground Storage. Violations are outstanding against API #: 105-21962: 35 P.S. 691.402(b); 25 PA; 78a.57(a); 35 P.S. 6018.301. See inspection report #3878285 for additional details.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Blackhill Energy's (Blackhill) Jackson A well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 4/10/2023 at 1525 hours. The weather was 67 degrees with clear skies. The inspection was conducted to evaluate remedial activities that were conducted after a release that occurred on 4/6/2023.Moody and Associates Inc. (Moody's)(Environmental consultant) was onsite during my inspection and have been conducting field screenings for Blackhill. Since the release that occurred on 4/6/2023, Blackhill has had the entire southern stormwater conveyance channel excavated (photos #2, 3 and 4). Blackhill reported that soil readings in the channel were now field measured below 1.0mS/cm. Excavation points on both sides of the access road culvert are now acting as sumps for the collection of residual fluids. A water truck was stationed at these points today, recovering any collected fluids. The pad surface area that was determined to be impacted by the release has been excavated as much as possible (photos #6 and 7). Blackhill explained that collected fluids shown in photo #7 are also being recovered. Fluid in this area, which is located right next to the initial release point, was field measured at ~17.8mS/cm today. Blackhill reported that equipment will be brought in on either 4/11/2023 or 4/12/2023 to move the produced water tanks and associated secondary containment structure in order to excavate beneath them. The impacted stormwater basin has been emptied to where just a few puddles remain (photo #1). All water collected from the basin was stored in tanks shown in photo #9 and continues to be trucked offsite for disposal or reuse. I field measured a small puddle near the stormwater channel entry point of the basin which returned a reading of ~1.75mS/cm. All impacted materials that have been recovered are stored in lined and covered waste containers which are held on secondary containment (photo #8). All violations associated with the releases from 1/2/2023 and from 4/6/2023 remain outstanding at this time against API #015-23733. I departed the site at 1620 hours.As a follow-up to the violations cited on 4/6/2023, the DEP requests a summary of the quantity of fluids collected in regards to the produced water release, including the stormwater basin, and where the water was transported after collection. This information can be provided in the NOV response.

The water in the southwest stormwater vault was about 6 feet from the top of the vault. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 21.9 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 24 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 24 uS/cm. Stream site names have been reorganized by STL Resources consults. The numbers in parentheses at the end of the site names are the original numbers and the number outside the parentheses are the current numbers.Three monitoring wells have been drilled about 50 yards to the west of the well pad. All the infiltration berms at the site have been hydro seeded. The percent vegetated cover varies from berm to berm. The recently rebuilt northwest and southwest infiltration berms at the well pad are beginning to become vegetated. The water in the northwest infiltration berm was screened for conductivity and resulted in 230 uS/cm.No new violations noted. Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 957721
Permit API: 063-34032
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Cherryhill Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/02/2022
Comments: On 6/2/22 at 0900 hrs., I conducted an inspection of Turm Oil, Inc.'s Paul Strong 4 well (API 063-34032) in Cherryhill Twp., Indiana Co. Mr. Bill Davis with Turm Oil was also present during the inspection. The inspection was conducted in response to a complaint, received by the Department on 6/1/22, of oil and produced water being released from a production fluids tank that was being removed from the site.I spoke with the complainant, the operator, and Mr. Davis on 6/1/22. The operator informed me that the well was sold to Rosebud Mining back in March; however there is no record of a well transfer filed with the Department. During our phone call, Mr. Davis informed me that the tank removal and release occurred around 1100 hrs. on 5/31/22. He estimated that approximately 10 gallons of crude oil and production fluid was released when removing the tank, and stated that some absorbent material was placed near the well and was subsequently containerized. Mr. Davis also acknowledged that some released fluid was covered up during regrading of the site.Upon inspection of the site, oil stained soil and vegetation was observed, beginning at the regraded area of the well pad, and continuing along a drainage ditch adjacent to the pad. There was a strong crude oil odor present. The impacted water in the ditch flowed to a nearby ephemeral stream where a slight sheen was observed. The black plastic bag containing the absorbent material Mr. Davis previously applied was located at the base of the well head; however, no additional measures were taken to prevent the material from reaching Waters of the Commonwealth. I advised Mr. Davis to place absorbent boom or pads to prevent further downstream impacts. I also advised Mr. Davis that regulations require removal of the pollutant from the soil and water within 15 days. In addition, I requested that Mr. Davis reinstall a well tag with the permit number on the well head.The release was not reported to the Department. Violations of 91.33(A), 78.66(a), 91.34(A), 78.66(b), and78.66(e) are cited and will be immediately closed as 'unresolvable'.Violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), CSL 402(b), 78.54, 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(a), and SWMA 610(1) are being cited for the release of crude oil and production fluid onto the ground and into Waters of the Commonwealth. These violations will be resolved upon remediation and temporary stabilization of the site, and submission of waste manifests for the disposal of impacted material to the Department.

The Department contacted the operator via telephone at approximately 8:45 AM on May 18, 2020 to follow up. Based on this conversation, the operator stated that they believed a water truck was responsible for the leak, which went from the Production Tanks, across the pad, down the access road, and onto a public roadway. The Operator stated that remediation was completed by Sunday afternoon (May 17, 2020). The Operator mentioned that recorded video of the event from security cameras had probably caught the incident occurring. The Department is requesting any and all evidence that may have documented this incident. The Department is requesting additional information on the water truck including but not limited to, records of production fluid on the truck prior to accessing the site, how much was removed from the Production Tanks at Prentice, and the total that was off loaded after leaving the Prentice site to be submitted to the Department by 5/29/2020. The Department is also requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted as soon as possible. Photos attached to this inspection were provided by the operator. Based on this inspection, violations are being noted as immediately corrected. Pending the operator's response, and further investigation, more violations may be issued.

Comments: Due to COVID-19 restrictions, an admin inspection is being conducted. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2/06/2023 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/06/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 984605
Permit API: 081-21879
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/06/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification received on February 3, 2023 from the operator of a release of produced fluid to the pad surface and access road of Pad B from clam boxes which were being removed from the location. Two snubbing units are in operation on Pad B. I met with company man Josh Scheihing upon arriving on Pad B. He showed me where on the access road the release had occurred. The surface had already been scraped at the time of this inspection. No fluid was observed in this area. Some clam shell boxes were present along the access road near the area that had been scraped. According to the operator, these boxes were empty and were slated to be removed. I walked the rest of the site with the company man. The fluid in the sump at the northeast stormwater channel outlet was frozen. There was snow and ice present in the northeast corner of the pad but no fluid was observed. The majority of the pad surface was dry or had snow and ice on it. I found an area along the east side of the pad with fluid with an electrical conductivity (EC) of greater than 19.99 mS/cm near a trailer for MidAtlantic Energy Services. The farther away from the trailer I took EC readings, the more the EC decreased. At the farthest north point of the fluid puddle, the EC was 1977 uS/cm and at the farther point to the south the EC was 2.74 mS/cm. I took sample 0718-203 from the area next to the MidAtlantic Energy Services trailer to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Br, Li, and Al. I let the company man know what I found before leaving the location. I called Rick Hall of EQT on the same day after leaving the location to let him know what I found. On the same day, Zac Subra of EQT sent me an email which stated that they had done their own investigation on the pad and had found out that MidAtlantic Energy Services used ice melt to melt the ice around their trailer. EQT believes that this caused the elevated electrical conductivity. The email included photos of the ice melt used. Also on the same day the operator notified the Department that fluid with a high electrical conductivity was found beneath rig mats on the pad. The notification stated that the operator believed that this fluid may be associated with the release from the clam shell boxes which occurred on 2/3/23 since the clam shells had been stored on the dancefloor prior to being moved off of the pad. The operator estimated the volume of this fluid at 42 gallons. Due to the estimated volume of the release, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation for this release.Violations noted for the release from the clam shell boxes to Pad B and the Pad B access road.

Report Details
Operator: Minard Run Oil Co
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-08-20
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 859451
Permit API: 053-27204
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Jenks Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-08-20
Comments: Site of oil release reported on 6/21/2019 was from the secondary containment of a tank battery located east off Salmon Road in a forested area. Oil was released from a hole in the bottom of one of the tanks located in a plastic lined secondary containment. An estimated several barrels of oil were released into the secondary containment. The valved discharge pipe through the secondary containment embankment was open for an unknown period of time after the tank was breached allowing the flow of an estimated one barrel of oil to be released to the ditch north of the tank battery. The oil released into the ditch flowed through a culvert under the access road and continued to spread out and flow through vegetation approximately 400 feet. Moody & Associates has been employed to coordinate the clean-up of this crude oil release. Jordan Sipos, P.G. completed the testing to establish the extent of the release and contaminated soil. Clean-up of the contaminated soil appears to be completed. Soil removal has been extended several hundred feet north of the area originally flagged as showing oil contamination from the release. Four piles of contaminated soil have been secured adjacent to the clean-up area until testing has been completed for disposal. A temporary road has been stoned to access the area and for the eventual removal of the contaminated soil. Manifest for the removal and disposal of the contaminated soil need to be submitted to the Department to lift the violations associated with this release. The removal of the contaminated soil was completed with the least disturbance possible to the surrounding vegetation and without creating a muddy unstable area. Replacement of topsoil and vegetation of this area needs to be coordinated with landowner and State Forest representatives. 15 Day initial Response Letter received July 1, 2019 for Alternate Remediation provision found in the PA DEP Oil and Gas Spill Policy. The report for the clean-up and restoration of the area needs to be submitted to the Department and approved before violations can be lifted.
